JEZIEL S. EMBODO, CPA Municipal Accountant Municipality of Padada Province of Davao del Sur Dear Ms. Embodo: This is in reference to your letter dated 12 February 2019 to Dir. Alex C. Roldan, Regional Director, DILG Region XI inquiring on whether Acting Liga President Emma G. Boncawel is entitled to the salary of an ex-officio member of the Sangguniang Bayan (SB). At the outset, in your query on whether Ms. Bongcawel is entitled to the salary Of the ex-officio Member of the SB, we reply in negative. The assumption of Acting Liga President Boncawel of the duties and functions of the Office of the ex-officio member of the SB is already included in her duties when she was proclaimed as Vice President of the Liga ng mga Barangay. Hence, it is only an additional imposition of obligation or a designation because the incumbent is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties. The said additional function or duty does not entitle her to any further remuneration.l This additional duty is also explicit in the 2017 Liga ng mga Barangay Constitution and By Laws, viz: Article VIII, Section 2 (b). The VIZe President 1. If for any reason, the president is unable to perform his duties, the executive vice president shall perform the duties orthe president subject to the rules of succession provided in sec. 2, article XII herein; Moreover, the Supreme Court in the case of Dimaandal vs Commission on Audit2 said that: "There is a great difference between an appointment and designation. I'Vhi/e an appointment is the selection by the proper authority of an individual who is to exercise the powers and functions of a given office, designation merely connotes an imposition of additional duties. usually bylaw. upon a person already in the public service by virtue of an earlier appointment (Santiago vs. COA, 199 SCRA 125). 1 DILG Opinion No 18, s. 2001 dated 26 March 2001 G.R. No. 112197, June 26, 1998

Designation is simply the mere imposition of new or additional duties on the officer or employee to be performed by him in a special does not entail payment of additional benefits or grant upen the person so designated the right to claim the salary attached to the pesition (COA Decision No. 95-087 dated February Z 1995). As such, there being no appointment issued. designation does not entitle the officer designated to receive the salary oftheposition. For the legal basis of an employees right to claim the salary attached thereto is a duly issued and approved appointment to the position (Opinion dated January 25, 1994 of the Office for Legal Affairs, Civil Service Commission, Re: Evora, Carlos, A. yr., Designation). However, Hon. Bongcawel is entitled of the RATA of the Office of an ex-officio Member of the SB as she is actually performing the duties and functions therein. An employee whose position is not authorized by law to collect the same but is designated to a position vacated temporarily by the incumbent on account of his leave of absence, and other legal cause shall be entitled to the regular RATA of the position on reimbursable basis provided he is duly designated by the appointing authority. 3 Lastly, we stand with our position in DILG Opinion No. 20, s. 2018 which impliedly amend DILG Opinion No. 4, s. 2005. We hope we had addressed your concerns accordingly. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MARI L C. SACENDONCILLO, CESO 111 Un ersecretary for Local Government Copy furnished: Dir. Alex C.
